research.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
research.why: Highest general-reader significance in the pool: finding a few doctored seconds hidden inside an otherwise real long video is the realistic deepfake threat, and it is easy to explain. Not covered in the last 8 weeks. arXiv abstract page is the primary source. The scout summarized from the HF abstract only, so the writer must read the paper (method, dataset, numbers) before drafting.

news.title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis
news.why: Clearly the most significant story in the window. Two labs say models refuted a central conjecture in complexity theory. Merge the Oct 26 OpenAI 'three discoveries plus academic program' item into it. Not covered before: the Oct 24 issue was about formal software verification, not this result. Caveat: the scout could not fetch the OpenAI page. The writer must check the claim against a fetchable primary source (try the Anthropic formal-math repo, which may hold the machine-checked proof, then the OpenAI page) and include expert caveats from TechCrunch and The Verge. If neither primary source can be fetched, fall back to the runner-up.

runnersUp.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
runnersUp.note: Significant safety story, but no Anthropic primary found and exact date unconfirmed.

Anthropic files for its public debut

invention.title: Hob: open-source desktop app that runs a Cowork-style file agent entirely on local open-weight models
invention.why: Most significant and useful build in the window: a private, offline file agent on your own hardware under the MIT license, plus a real lesson that small models' tool calls needed code guards, not better prompts. Strong HN signal (164 pts, 42 comments, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50246238). Caveat: the repo page was not fetchable and the details come from the author's HN post. The writer must confirm the license, platforms and model list from the repo or README before drafting. If that fails, use ADRs for AI.

thread: Each pick is about checking AI output rather than trusting it: machine-checked proofs behind a big math claim, forensics that find a few faked seconds in a real video, and code guards that stop small local models from making bad tool calls.
